key: Watching someone ride a bike
name: ch00_bike_lecture_vs_practice
alt: A boy watches a cycling demonstration from a bench on the left, while on the right he wobbles and falls off a bicycle and gets back up.
scene: A wide two-part scene on a dusty Indian housing-colony lane at late afternoon, separated by a thin vertical line. LEFT half: a boy of about ten in a white school shirt and navy shorts sits on a low cement bench with a notebook on his knees, chin resting on his hand, calmly watching his older cousin (about eighteen, grey T-shirt, rolled jeans) glide past on a black roadster bicycle with one hand raised as if explaining; small chalk arrows on the ground show the smooth straight path he rides, and the boy looks relaxed but passive. RIGHT half: the same boy now on a small red bicycle, front wheel turned sharply, tipping sideways with one foot out and his mouth in a surprised O; a scraped knee with a small plaster is visible, and behind him a faint dotted trail of wobbly zig-zag tyre marks shows two earlier falls marked by little puff-of-dust shapes. Above the scene a mango tree, a parked scooter, a blue water tank on a roof and a neighbour aunty in a printed nightie smiling from a balcony. Warm golden light, gentle and encouraging mood. Labels: "LECTURE" at the top of the left half, "PROBLEM SET" at the top of the right half, and a small "WHERE YOU LEARN" tag with an arrow pointing to the dust puffs on the right.

key: A smoke alarm that stays silent
name: ch00_silent_smoke_alarm
alt: A quiet kitchen ceiling with a smoke alarm that is taped over and has a weak battery, while thin smoke drifts in from another room.
scene: A cutaway view of a small Indian apartment, seen like a dollhouse with the front wall removed, two rooms side by side. In the RIGHT room, a tidy kitchen with a steel gas stove, pressure cooker and spice dabba, a round white smoke alarm is fixed to the ceiling, completely silent; on it three small inset bubbles point to its possible faults: a strip of brown parcel tape stuck across its grille, a battery icon showing one thin red bar, and a tiny dotted arrow showing it is in the wrong room. In the LEFT room, a bedroom with a steel almirah and a ceiling fan, a thin grey curl of smoke rises from a forgotten mosquito coil near a curtain, drifting toward the ceiling where no alarm is fitted. A middle-aged man in a vest and lungi sits in the doorway between the rooms reading a newspaper with a calm, unaware expression, a cup of chai beside him, trusting the quiet. Soft evening tube-light glow, mostly calm with a faint undertone of unease. Labels: "SILENCE" in a speech-bubble shape beside the kitchen alarm, "NO EVIDENCE" above the bedroom smoke, and a short "TRUST THE ALARM?" floating above the man with a question mark.

key: A crowded cinema where someone shouts
name: ch01_cinema_fire_panic
alt: Panicking moviegoers jam a single cinema exit door, their rush to escape being exactly what blocks it.
scene: An interior view of an old single-screen Indian cinema hall at night, seen from slightly above the back rows, the big screen glowing pale blue at the top of the frame. In the foreground right, a lone usher in a maroon uniform with a torch has just shouted, one hand cupped to his mouth. Dozens of moviegoers of all ages — a college student in a hoodie, a mother in a green salwar holding a toddler, an elderly man with a walking stick, two office workers still holding popcorn cups — have all leapt from their red folding seats and surge toward a single narrow exit door on the left lit by a green sign. At the doorway they are jammed shoulder to shoulder, arms raised, faces strained, nobody actually getting through; popcorn spills across the aisle. Bold curved arrows from every row converge on the door and then turn into a tight knot of tangled lines at the door frame. A small inset circle in the upper left shows a trader at a laptop with his finger hovering over a red SELL button, sweating, linked by a dotted line to the crowd. Dim theatre lighting with a warm red glow from the exit sign, tense and chaotic mood. Labels: "EVERYONE SELLS" above the crowd, "THE LOW" on the jammed door frame.

key: roulette edge is under 3%, yet a casin
name: ch01_casino_small_edge
alt: A casino roulette table where one lucky player wins tonight while a long ledger shows the house winning over millions of spins.
scene: A warm, slightly cinematic view of a roulette table in a Goa riverboat casino at night, the camera at table height. At the centre, a polished wooden roulette wheel spins with a white ball blurring around the rim. On the left, a cheerful young man in a loud floral shirt raises both fists, a tall stack of chips sliding toward him, his friends behind him cheering. On the right, a calm croupier in a black waistcoat and bow tie, mid-thirties, neat bun, pushes the chips across without any concern, her face perfectly neutral. Behind her, mounted on the wall, a long scroll-like ledger unrolls down to the floor, covered in tiny tally marks, with a gently rising line drawn across the whole length and a small counter reading "SPIN 4,812,330". In a small inset bubble near the bottom left, a lone trader at a desk with a much shorter ledger of just a few tally marks looks at a wobbly, uncertain line. Lighting from overhead brass lamps, reflections in the dark window showing river lights, mood confident and unhurried. Labels: "HOUSE EDGE" on the ledger, "LUCK" above the cheering player, "FEW SPINS" on the inset trader.

key: Two people learning the guitar
name: ch01_two_guitar_learners
alt: Two guitar students: one with a guitar leaning untouched in a corner, the other practising the same hard chord in every room of his house.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a small Indian flat in the evening. LEFT panel: a young man of about twenty in a yellow T-shirt lies on a sofa scrolling his phone, a TV glowing; his acoustic guitar leans in the corner with a faint layer of dust and a cobweb strand between the tuning pegs, and a wall calendar beside it has only two practice days ticked in the whole month. RIGHT panel: a second young man of the same age in a maroon kurta is shown three times in one continuous house cutaway — in the kitchen with the guitar strapped on while waiting for the kettle, on the balcony at dusk, and on his bed late at night — always pressing the same awkward barre chord with a focused, slightly frustrated frown; tiny red X marks float near the strings for buzzing notes and a single green tick appears in the last scene where the chord rings clean. His calendar is full of ticks. Both panels share the same music teacher's printed sheet pinned to the wall. Warm lamp light, encouraging mood. Labels: "PLAYS WHEN FREE" at the top of the left panel, "DELIBERATE PRACTICE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A pianist rehearsing a sonata gets
name: ch01_pianist_vs_firefighter
alt: A pianist calmly rehearsing the same piece contrasted with a firefighter facing an unpredictable blaze, with the trader closer to the firefighter.
scene: A split-panel scene divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a quiet music room with a black upright piano, a woman pianist in her thirties in a simple cream saree sits upright playing from a sheet whose page shows the same printed notes; behind her, three faded ghost copies of herself at the same piano suggest identical rehearsals on previous nights, and a tidy metronome ticks. Soft lamp light, serene. RIGHT panel: at night on a narrow old-city street with overhead tangled wires, a firefighter in a heavy khaki-and-yellow suit and helmet, about forty, braces with a hose against an orange blaze bursting from a shop's upper floor; smoke shapes curl unpredictably, a falling signboard and a sudden flare from a gas cylinder are shown with small warning bursts, and his face is calm and steady despite the danger. Between the panels, at the bottom, a small trader at a laptop with candlestick screen sits on a stool placed clearly on the right side of the dividing line, closer to the firefighter, glancing toward the flames. Contrast warm calm light on the left with flickering orange on the right. Labels: "SAME NOTES" above the piano, "NEW FIRE EVERY TIME" above the firefighter, "TRADING" on a small tag on the trader's stool.

key: A first-order pivot high is a single
name: ch02_queue_tall_people
alt: A railway ticket queue where some people stand taller than their neighbours and one stands taller than the other tall ones.
scene: A side-on, eye-level view of a long queue of about fifteen people standing in a line outside an Indian railway reservation counter, a yellow-and-black station sign and a ticket window grille on the far right. The people are deliberately varied in height: short schoolgirls, average office-goers, an elderly lady with a cloth bag, a man with a suitcase on his head. Four of them are noticeably taller than the person on either side — a tall college boy in a cricket cap, a lanky man in a white kurta, a woman in a red saree with her hair in a high bun, and a very tall security guard in khaki. Small orange triangle markers float above these four. One of them, the tall guard near the middle, is also taller than the tall people before and after him, and gets a larger double-triangle marker plus a dotted bracket connecting the four tall heads to show the second level of comparison. The background has a station clock, a chai stall and a wall poster. Bright midday light, crisp shadows on the platform floor, light-hearted everyday mood. Labels: "FIRST-ORDER" with a small arrow to one of the single orange triangles, "SECOND-ORDER" next to the guard's double marker.

key: Support is a trampoline that
name: ch02_worn_trampoline_support
alt: A worn backyard trampoline sagging more with each jump until its fabric finally tears.
scene: A wide scene in a residential compound in the evening, showing the same old backyard trampoline four times from left to right in a single continuous strip, like a time-lapse. In each frame a cheerful boy of about twelve in a blue jersey and shorts drops onto it. FRAME 1: taut black fabric, the boy springs high with arms up, a large curved arrow showing a strong bounce. FRAME 2: the fabric now visibly sags in the middle, springs slightly stretched, the bounce arrow is shorter and the boy looks less excited. FRAME 3: the mat sags deeply, a few springs dangle loose, the boy lands with knees bent and only rises a little, a small worried look on his face, a dotted arrow shows him coming in fast. FRAME 4: the fabric has torn open in a jagged hole, the boy is dropping through to the grass below with a startled expression, legs dangling, a small cloud of dust. Two neighbourhood kids watch from a low wall on the right, and a guava tree and drying clothes line fill the background. Warm sunset light, playful but with a building sense of strain. Labels: "SUPPORT" on the fabric in frame 1, "WEAKER BOUNCES" spanning frames 2–3, "THE BREAK" above the torn hole in frame 4.

key: You see a neighbour carrying an umbrella
name: ch02_neighbour_umbrella
alt: A man at his window sees a neighbour carrying an umbrella and assumes rain, while thought bubbles show other possible reasons.
scene: A view across a narrow lane between two old three-storey Mumbai chawl-style buildings on a bright, mostly clear morning. In the foreground left, a curious middle-aged man in a white banian with spectacles leans out of his window, holding a newspaper, looking down with raised eyebrows; above him a thought cloud shows a dark rain cloud and raindrops. Down in the lane, his neighbour, a tidy older gentleman in a grey safari suit, walks briskly carrying a large black umbrella, closed and hooked over his arm. Around the neighbour float three small inset bubbles showing what might really be going on: one shows him handing the umbrella back to a friend at a door, one shows the umbrella open as a sunshade against a bright sun, and one shows him simply glancing nervously at the sky out of caution. A single thin arrow from the umbrella points to a small chalk-board sign in the corner of the frame. The rest of the lane has a vegetable cart, potted tulsi plants and laundry on balconies. Bright morning light, gently humorous mood. Labels: "VISIBLE ACTION" with an arrow to the umbrella, "HIDDEN REASON" above the three bubbles, and the chalk-board reads "BIG PUT BUY".

key: a stone thrown into a pond
name: ch02_stone_pond_ripples
alt: Stones dropped into a calm village pond create ripples that shrink slowly, with a pebble thrown just after a boulder still making big waves.
scene: A calm village pond at dawn seen from a low angle near the stone steps of a small ghat, a banyan tree and a little white temple on the far bank, lotus leaves floating near the edge. In the centre-left, a large boulder has just splashed into the water, sending up a tall crown of spray, with a series of wide concentric rings spreading out and slowly getting smaller toward the edges, each ring drawn slightly fainter. On the right, a smaller pebble is falling into the still-agitated rings of the boulder, and its own ripples combine with the big ones to make tall, choppy waves. In a small inset circle in the lower left, the same pond is completely calm and a single tiny pebble makes only a faint ring that is barely visible. On the steps in the foreground sits a thoughtful boy of about eleven in a faded school uniform, one more pebble in his hand, watching the waves with interest; a brass lota and a bundle of washed clothes rest beside him. Soft pink dawn light and mist over the water, calm contemplative mood. Labels: "NEWS SHOCK" over the boulder splash, "VOLATILITY LINGERS" along the shrinking rings, "CALM POND" on the inset.

key: Two teams pushing a heavy cart
name: ch03_tug_cart_teams
alt: Two teams push a heavy wooden cart from opposite ends across lines drawn in the dirt, one clearly winning at first, then rocking back and forth.
scene: A wide, side-on view of a dusty village maidan in the afternoon, a heavy wooden bullock cart without bullocks loaded with sacks of grain in the centre. On the LEFT end, five sturdy men in vests and rolled-up dhotis push hard, leaning forward, sweating; on the RIGHT end, five young men in coloured T-shirts and track pants push back with equal effort. Across the ground run several white lime-powder lines, with older lines faded and scuffed out, and one freshly redrawn line just past the cart's front wheel where a small boy with a bucket of lime is crouching to redraw it. Faint ghosted wheel tracks show the cart rolled steadily right earlier, then rocked back and forth over a short stretch, drawn as a zig-zag trail of overlapping tyre marks. Far to the right, a single bold arrow shows the cart rolling well past the last line and continuing, with the right-hand team slumping in exhaustion. Villagers sit on a low wall watching, an old man with a walking stick acting as judge, a neem tree giving shade. Strong afternoon sun, energetic competitive mood. Labels: "TREND" over the earlier straight track, "RANGE" over the zig-zag rocking, "BREAKOUT" by the final arrow beyond the last line.

key: A crowded boat with everyone leaning
name: ch03_crowded_boat_lurch
alt: A crowded ferry with every passenger leaning on one side lurches when a wave hits, while one calm passenger stands near the exit.
scene: A side view of an overcrowded wooden river ferry crossing a wide brown river during the monsoon, low grey clouds overhead and a distant ghat with temples on the far bank. The first half of the scene, on the left, shows the boat gliding smoothly with almost every passenger — farmers with sacks, a woman with a goat, schoolchildren, a man with a bicycle — crowded onto the right-hand rail, the boat tilted but steady, calm water around it. On the right half of the scene, the same boat moments later: a single large wave slaps the hull, and everyone scrambles toward the opposite rail at once, arms flailing, a sack flying, the goat jumping, the boat lurching sharply with a big splash; curved motion arrows show the whole crowd shifting together. In both moments, one calm passenger — a thin older man in a white kurta and grey shawl holding a small cloth bag — stands quietly beside the boarding gap near the stern, one hand on the rail, ready to step off. Dramatic monsoon light with a sliver of sun breaking through, tense mood. Labels: "CROWDED TRADE" over the leaning passengers, "ONE WAVE" by the splash, "NEAR THE EXIT" with an arrow to the calm man.

key: Surfing. The waves (market cycles)
name: ch03_surfer_reading_sets
alt: A surfer paddles hard when good waves arrive and rests on the beach when the sea is flat or choppy.
scene: A wide beach scene at Varkala-style cliffs on India's southwest coast, red laterite cliffs on the right with small cafés on top, coconut palms leaning over. The sea stretches across the frame from left to right in three zones. LEFT zone: a set of clean, evenly spaced green waves rolls in, and a lean young woman surfer in a black rash vest and board shorts, mid-twenties, paddles hard on a white board with a determined face, a curved arrow showing her catching the wave. MIDDLE zone: messy choppy water with whitecaps going in all directions, a second surfer is tumbling off his board with a splash, looking frustrated. RIGHT zone: the sea is flat and glassy, and the same woman now sits relaxed on the sand under a palm with her board stuck upright beside her, sipping tender coconut water, watching the water patiently. A small inset bubble near the top shows a simple heart-rate-style wave line labelled to suggest her own good and bad days. Late-morning sun, bright turquoise and sandy tones, calm but alert mood. Labels: "PADDLE HARD" above the left zone, "CHOP: SIT OUT" above the middle, "WAIT ON THE BEACH" above the right.

key: An auction where the last bidder jumps
name: ch03_mandi_last_bidder
alt: At a mandi auction the last bidder jumps the price wildly to win, leaving nobody behind him to buy at that price.
scene: A busy open-air Indian vegetable mandi auction yard in the early morning, piles of onion sacks and crates of tomatoes in rows, a tin shed roof overhead. In the centre, the auctioneer, a stout man in his fifties with a white Gandhi cap and a notepad, points dramatically at one bidder. That bidder, a young trader in a flashy shiny shirt and gold chain, stands on an onion sack with his arm raised high, shouting, clearly jumping far above everyone else; a large bold upward arrow rises from his hand. Behind him, the crowd of other buyers — older traders in kurtas and shawls, a woman wholesaler with a ledger, a porter with a head-load — have all lowered their hands, shrugging or turning away, some already walking off. On the right edge of the frame, a second small scene shows the next lot of onions, with only one buyer left half-heartedly raising a finger and a small downward arrow beside the price board, which reads a clearly lower number. Bright early sun slanting through dust and onion skins, energetic but slightly absurd mood. Labels: "BUYING CLIMAX" above the jumping bidder, "NO ONE LEFT" over the turned-away crowd, "LOWER PRICE" by the right-hand board.

key: Learning to see pullbacks is like
name: ch04_birdwatching_bad_light
alt: A birdwatcher with a guidebook peers through mist at a half-hidden bird, learning to recognise it in poor light.
scene: A misty early-morning wetland scene like a bird sanctuary in Bharatpur, tall reeds in the foreground, a few bare acacia trees in the middle distance and soft grey fog everywhere. On the left foreground, a young birdwatcher in her twenties wearing an olive jacket, cap and binoculars around her neck kneels in the reeds, holding an open bird guidebook with a crisp coloured illustration of a kingfisher on the page. Her eyes are not on the book but squinting through the fog at the actual bird, which is half hidden among leaves on a branch to the right: only a dull blue wing, part of a beak and one eye are visible, much less clear than the book's picture. A dotted line connects the book's picture to the real bird with a question-mark tag. Behind her, faint ghost silhouettes of dozens of other birds she has already logged are lined up like a filmstrip. In the far background a sheet of fog covers the horizon like a curtain so the future is unseen. Cool blue-grey dawn light, quiet patient mood. Labels: "RULE SHEET" on the guidebook, "REAL CHART" pointing to the half-hidden bird, "NO PEEKING" on the fog curtain.

key: A good detective writes down in advance
name: ch04_detective_clearing_evidence
alt: A detective writes down in advance the evidence that would clear a suspect and looks for it, while a careless colleague collects only evidence that fits.
scene: A split-panel scene set inside a cluttered Indian police station office with a ceiling fan, steel filing cabinets and a framed map of the city. LEFT panel: an experienced woman detective in her forties, crisp khaki uniform, reading glasses on a chain, stands at a cork board where a suspect's photo silhouette is pinned. Beside the photo she has pinned an index card listing what would clear him, and she is carefully comparing a fingerprint card with a magnifying glass, a fair, sceptical expression. A small stack of evidence against her theory is piling up on the desk, labelled with neat tags. RIGHT panel: a younger, overconfident officer with slicked hair and a big moustache pins only papers that support his theory to a board, red string all going one way, while a pile of contrary papers lies ignored in the waste bin under his desk; he looks smug and does not notice. Light from a tall barred window falls across both desks, dust floating in the beam. Neutral, thoughtful mood with a hint of humour on the right. Labels: "GOOD DETECTIVE" at the top of the left panel, "BAD DETECTIVE" at the top of the right panel, and "EVIDENCE AGAINST" on the growing pile on the left desk.

key: A dog on a long lead. The lead
name: ch04_dog_long_lead
alt: A dog on a long lead runs to the end of it, and its owner waits for the dog to drift back before walking on together.
scene: A wide scene along a seaside promenade like Marine Drive in the morning, a curved sea wall, distant buildings and a few joggers in the background. In the centre-left, a calm man in his thirties wearing a white T-shirt, track pants and running shoes stands still holding the handle of a very long retractable lead. The lead stretches tight to the right where a golden Indian pariah dog has sprinted ahead and hit the end of the lead, front paws off the ground, ears flying, tongue out. A faint dotted outline of a wide corridor drawn on the pavement around the man shows how far the lead allows the dog to roam. In a second ghosted moment to the right, the same dog has wandered back close to the man's legs, sniffing the ground, and then a final position shows both of them walking together toward the right, the man stepping forward with a relaxed smile. Small curved arrows show the sequence: run out, drift back, walk on. Seagulls, a chai vendor with a cycle and a parked scooter fill the background. Soft morning sun and sea breeze, calm and patient mood. Labels: "BAND" on the dotted corridor, "STRONG RUN" at the dog at full stretch, "ENTER HERE" at the moment the dog returns.

key: Parking on a hill. You leave a gap
name: ch04_hill_parking_gap
alt: Cars parked on a steep hill road, with a driver leaving the right gap behind the car in front, one too-close car getting bumped and one too-far wasting space.
scene: A steep hill-station road like in Shimla, lined with colourful houses stepped up the slope, pine trees and a misty valley behind. Three small cars are parked nose-uphill along the kerb, each behind another car, shown as three side-by-side situations from left to right. LEFT: a white hatchback parked almost touching the car ahead; the car ahead has rolled back slightly and its bumper is nudging it, with a small crash star and an annoyed driver in a sweater throwing up his hands. CENTRE: a blue sedan with a perfectly measured gap behind the car in front; a middle-aged woman driver in a shawl calmly pulls the handbrake, and a short measuring tape lies on the road showing the gap, with a small dotted ghost of the front car rolling back a little and stopping safely short. RIGHT: a red car parked so far back that a large empty stretch of road sits wasted in front of it, a frustrated man circling in another car with no place to park. A small inset bubble shows a ruler marking how much cars usually roll on this slope. Crisp cool mountain light, gently humorous mood. Labels: "TOO TIGHT" on the left, "STOP DISTANCE" on the measured gap in the centre, "WASTED ROOM" on the right.

key: A classic pullback is a runner pausing
name: ch05_runner_turns_uphill
alt: One runner pauses for water mid-race, while another who was jogging downhill suddenly sprints uphill and stops for the first time.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves on a hilly road race through the Nilgiri tea gardens with rows of green tea bushes and silver oak trees. LEFT panel: a marathon runner in her thirties wearing a red vest with a race number pauses at a water station mid-race, sipping from a paper cup handed by a volunteer in a white T-shirt, still facing the same direction as the long line of runners heading up the road; a solid arrow shows the race continuing the same way. RIGHT panel: a lean young man in a green vest is shown in a short sequence along a winding road: first jogging downhill with relaxed arms (a faint arrow pointing down the slope), then suddenly sprinting hard uphill with fists pumping and a determined grimace, then stopping for his first breather at a bend, hands on knees, looking up the hill. A small curved arrow at the bend has a question mark, asking whether he will keep going up. Fresh morning light and low clouds over the hills. Labels: "PULLBACK" at the top of the left panel, "ANTI" at the top of the right panel, and "FIRST PAUSE" with a small arrow to the man resting at the bend.

key: A level is less like a wall
name: ch05_muddy_riverbank_level
alt: A ball rolling toward a muddy riverbank bounces off, sinks in, or rolls into the water, while a walker discovers the clean line is a messy strip up close.
scene: A wide scene of a river during the post-monsoon season, a broad brown river on the right and a sloping muddy bank on the left with grass and a few tree roots. Far in the background on the left, a small figure stands on a hill looking through binoculars, and from that distance the bank appears as a clean straight line drawn in white. In the foreground, the bank is shown up close as a wide, uneven strip of mud with puddles, footprints and tufts of grass. Three footballs roll down the slope toward the bank, each with a dotted trail: the first bounces cleanly off a hard edge and back up the slope; the second sinks into soft mud, gets stuck, then slowly climbs out with a small dotted path; the third rolls straight past the bank and splashes into the river. A boy of about nine in a striped T-shirt chases the balls barefoot, laughing, and an old fisherman mending nets on an upturned boat watches. Soft late-afternoon light, earthy and playful mood. Labels: "LEVEL FROM FAR" near the white line in the distance, "MESSY ZONE" across the muddy strip.

key: until you know how many patients who
name: ch05_doctor_control_group
alt: A doctor proudly shows patients who took his pill, while an auditor points at the much larger group of patients who did not take it and were also fine.
scene: A busy hospital corridor in an Indian district hospital, green-painted walls, a wall clock and a bench along one side. On the left, a confident doctor in his fifties with a white coat, stethoscope and thick moustache gestures proudly to a group of five smiling patients holding small pill bottles, all healthy and waving, and a calendar on the wall shows one full year crossed off. On the right, a calm young woman researcher in a lab coat with a clipboard points to a second, larger group of patients standing on the other side of a dotted dividing line, people who never took the pill, who are also smiling and healthy — an elderly man with a cane, a pregnant woman, a farmer, a schoolboy. Small number cards held up by each group show similar ratios of well people. The doctor's proud expression is starting to falter as he glances right. Nurses push a trolley in the background. Bright tube-light lighting with sun through a barred window, light, slightly comic mood. Labels: "PILL GROUP" above the left patients, "CONTROL GROUP" above the right patients, "BASELINE" on the researcher's clipboard.

key: A sprinter running with a strong
name: ch05_sprinter_tailwind_shoelace
alt: A sprinter with a strong tailwind stops to tie a shoelace; if she starts again at once the wind is still strong, if she lingers maybe it has dropped.
scene: A seaside running track along a beach road at dusk, palm trees bent toward the right by a strong wind, flags on poles flapping hard to the right and sand blowing in streaks. A determined young woman sprinter in her early twenties, wearing a blue running vest and black shorts with her hair in a tight braid, has stopped mid-run and is crouching on one knee to tie the lace of her right shoe. Large soft white wind arrows sweep across the whole frame from left to right behind her, pushing her direction of travel. Two small inset bubbles float above her: in the LEFT bubble she springs straight back up and sprints off to the right with the wind arrows still bold and strong; in the RIGHT bubble she is still standing around, hands on hips, and the wind arrows have faded to faint thin lines and the flags hang limp. A coach in a tracksuit with a stopwatch watches from a bench, one eyebrow raised. Warm orange sunset light with long shadows, focused and expectant mood. Labels: "BIGGER TREND" on the wind arrows, "NESTED PAUSE" pointing to the crouching sprinter, and "WIND DROPPED?" on the right bubble.

key: Someone pushes a door that looks locked
name: ch06_door_rattle_failure
alt: A crowd leaning on a locked door expecting it to burst open stumbles backward when it only rattles and stays shut.
scene: An old government office building corridor in India with tall wooden doors, peeling cream paint, a brass nameplate and a ceiling fan. In the centre, a heavy double wooden door with an iron padlock and chain looks locked. A burly man in a checked shirt has just thrown his shoulder against it, and the door only rattles: small vibration lines and a shake-burst around the chain, but no gap opens. Behind him, a line of six eager people — a college student, a clerk with files, a woman with a handbag, two young men in office ID lanyards, an elderly man — had been leaning forward on each other's backs expecting to fall through, and now they all stumble backward in a domino chain, arms flailing, files and papers flying, one man's spectacles slipping off. On the far left of the frame, a calm woman in a blue salwar watches with arms folded and a knowing half-smile, already turning to walk the other way, with a small arrow pointing back down the corridor. Dusty afternoon light through a tall window, comic and slightly chaotic mood. Labels: "BREAKOUT ATTEMPT" above the door, "TRAPPED BUYERS" over the stumbling crowd, "FAILURE TEST" by the calm woman.

key: A lab notebook. You can write tomorrow
name: ch06_lab_notebook_ink
alt: A scientist writes results in ink in a bound lab notebook while another tries to rub out failed runs and ends up with blank pages.
scene: A split-panel scene inside a modest research laboratory with glass beakers, a fume hood and a window showing a campus with neem trees. LEFT panel: a careful young woman scientist in her late twenties, white lab coat over a printed kurta, safety glasses pushed up on her head, writes in a thick bound notebook with a fountain pen; the open pages are filled with dated entries, small sketches and several results crossed with a single neat line but still readable, including one marked with a red X for a failed run. A coffee mug and a calculator sit beside her. Her expression is calm and honest. RIGHT panel: a nervous young man in a lab coat with messy hair frantically rubs at his notebook with a big pink eraser, eraser crumbs piling up on the bench; most of his pages are now blank or smudged grey, with only one proud tick left. A wastebasket beside him overflows with crumpled pages. A flask behind him bubbles over unnoticed. Clean white lab lighting with soft daylight from the window. Labels: "INK STAYS" at the top of the left panel, "ERASED RUNS" at the top of the right panel, "NO RESULT" with an arrow to the blank pages.

key: Squint at a crowd from a balcony
name: ch06_balcony_vs_crowd
alt: One trader watches a festival crowd from a balcony seeing its direction, while another stands in the crowd reading individual faces.
scene: A busy Indian festival street during a Ganesh Chaturthi procession, seen from above at an angle, marigold garlands strung across the lane, drums and colourful flags. On the upper right, a calm man in his forties wearing a white kurta and glasses stands on a first-floor balcony with a wrought-iron railing, holding a cup of chai, eyes slightly narrowed; from his viewpoint the crowd below is drawn as a mass of simple dots with large soft arrows all sweeping to the left along the street. Down in the crowd on the lower left, a younger woman in a yellow kurta with a notebook is pressed among people, turning her head to study individual faces up close — a drummer with puffed cheeks, a laughing girl on her father's shoulders, a vendor selling balloons — with small magnifying-glass bubbles around each face. A large decorated idol on a cart moves ahead in the distance. Warm evening light with orange powder in the air, festive and lively mood. Labels: "CONCEPTUAL TRADER" next to the man on the balcony, "DETAIL TRADER" next to the woman in the crowd, "DIRECTION" on the big crowd arrow.

key: A fire drill versus a real fire
name: ch06_fire_drill_vs_real
alt: Office workers only glance at the exit during a drill, while during a real fire alarm they run out, then rush back in.
scene: A split-panel scene of a tall glass office building in an Indian IT park, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a fire-drill bell rings softly on the wall of an open-plan office; employees at their desks — a young man with headphones, a woman with a laptop, a manager on a call — merely turn their heads toward the green exit sign, still seated, coffee cups in hand, mild bored expressions; a dotted arrow from their eyes to the exit shows only a glance. RIGHT panel: the same building from outside at ground level; a loud alarm with red flashing lines, people have sprinted out through the glass doors onto the lawn — some still holding laptops, one man missing a shoe, a security guard waving his arms — and then a big curved arrow shows a sudden rush back in through the doors once the all-clear is given, the crowd pushing back inside eagerly. A fire truck parked at the kerb with a firefighter leaning on it. Bright midday light, energetic and mildly comic mood. Labels: "THE GLANCE" at the top of the left panel, "REAL RUN" over the people on the lawn, "RUSH BACK IN" on the curved return arrow.

key: A crowd pressing on a gate
name: ch07_gate_three_positions
alt: People wait at a stadium gate in three positions: at the gate with tickets, running from nearby when it opens, and arriving after the crowd has settled.
scene: A wide scene outside a cricket stadium gate on match day in India, a tall iron gate with a security guard, banners, flags, and a crowd of fans in blue jerseys with painted faces pressing against it. The gate is just swinging open. Three positions are highlighted from left to right. FIRST, right at the bars, a young woman fan in a blue jersey holds up a printed ticket, pressed against the gate, first through the opening with a delighted grin. SECOND, a man in his thirties at a chai stall across the road hears the creak, drops his cup and sprints toward the gate, motion lines behind him, a little behind the leading crowd. THIRD, on the far right, a relaxed older man in a white shirt and cap strolls up much later after the crowd has already gone inside, the gate fully open and the road nearly empty, a few dropped flags on the ground. Above each person, a tiny ticket-price tag shows a different amount. Bright late-afternoon sun, excited match-day mood. Labels: "RESTING ORDER" over the woman at the gate, "SEE IT, THEN ACT" over the running man, "BAR CLOSE" over the late arrival.

key: A gold panner. The paper notebook is the
name: ch07_gold_panner_ideas
alt: A gold panner scoops river gravel with a shovel, washes it in a pan, and keeps the few gold flakes left at the bottom.
scene: A shallow rocky river in the foothills at morning, clear water flowing over pebbles, forested hills behind. A lean middle-aged prospector in a faded checked shirt, rolled trousers and a cloth tied around his head stands knee-deep in the stream. The scene flows left to right in three steps. On the left, a big pile of mixed sand and gravel on the bank next to a battered shovel stuck in it, with a spiral-bound paper notebook lying open on a rock beside it, pages filled with quick scribbles. In the centre, the man swirls a wide shallow pan in the water, muddy water and pebbles spilling over the rim, his face intently focused, and a small laptop-like tablet balanced on a dry rock nearby showing a short list. On the right, close-up, his palm holds the pan's bottom where a few shining gold flakes remain, and next to it on a flat stone sits a single neat index card with a gold border. Small arrows link the three steps. A kingfisher sits on a branch above. Bright, clear morning light glinting on water, patient and hopeful mood. Labels: "SCOOP EVERYTHING" on the left pile, "WASH AWAY" on the swirling pan, "SETUP SHEET" on the gold-bordered card.

key: A restaurant where the cook rewrites
name: ch07_cook_rewrites_recipe
alt: A cook keeps rewriting the recipe after every complaint while the owner insists the recipe be followed and the head chef reviews it monthly.
scene: Inside a busy small South Indian restaurant kitchen with large steel vessels, a dosa tawa, hanging ladles and a window into the dining room. On the left, a flustered young cook in a white vest and cap stands at a counter crossing out and rewriting a recipe card for the fifth time, a pile of crumpled cards at his feet, while through the service window a customer waves a complaint and another frowns at a plate. In the centre, the owner, a firm woman in her fifties in a cotton saree with spectacles, taps a laminated recipe card pinned to the wall and points sternly at it, holding a calendar in her other hand. On the right, at a small desk in the corner, an experienced head chef with a grey beard, tall white hat and reading glasses calmly reviews a thick folder of collected feedback slips, a wall calendar beside him with one date circled at the end of the month. Steam rises from pots and a ceiling fan turns. Warm yellow kitchen light, busy and slightly comic mood. Labels: "REWRITING EVERY DAY" over the flustered cook, "FOLLOW THE RECIPE" near the owner's card, "MONTHLY REVIEW" over the head chef's desk.

key: A boat on a river. The daily chart is
name: ch07_boat_waves_current
alt: A rower on a wide river rides small waves while a strong current flows the other way, with the decision made on the bank before setting out.
scene: A wide view of a broad river like the Brahmaputra at early morning, low mist, distant hills, and a sandy bank in the foreground. In the middle of the river, a fisherman in his forties in a vest and checked gamcha rows a narrow wooden country boat; small choppy waves under the boat are drawn with short arrows pointing to the right, while large, broad, faint arrows in the deeper water flow strongly to the left, showing the underlying current dragging the boat backwards despite his rowing. His face shows effort and slight worry. On the foreground bank, the same man is shown earlier, sitting calmly on the sand beside his beached boat with oars across his knees, looking out at the water and pointing in the current's direction while studying a stick map drawn in the sand; a dotted line connects this planning figure to the rower. Egrets stand in the shallows and a ferry crosses in the far distance. Pale golden misty light, thoughtful mood. Labels: "DAILY: WAVES" by the small arrows, "WEEKLY: CURRENT" along the big arrows, "DECIDE ON THE BANK" next to the planning figure.

key: Picking up coins in front of a
name: ch08_coins_steamroller
alt: A man happily picks up coins on a road in front of a slowly approaching steamroller.
scene: A long newly-tarred road under construction in an Indian city suburb, orange traffic cones, a hot haze, and a big yellow road roller crawling forward from the left side of the frame with a bored operator in a cap and sunglasses on top. Across the road ahead of the roller lies a scattering of shiny coins. In the centre-right, a cheerful man in his thirties wearing a striped shirt, trousers and sandals is bent over, happily picking coins and dropping them into a cloth pouch; behind him a small staircase of coin stacks on the kerb grows steadily higher, one stack per week, each with a tiny date flag. The roller's front drum is very close behind him, just a couple of steps away, but he is not looking back. On the far right, a small inset bubble shows the outcome for an unlucky version of him: the coin stacks flattened into a single long dent in the tar and his sandals left behind. Construction workers in hard hats on the side watch with alarm, one pointing. Harsh noon sunlight, sweaty and darkly comic mood. Labels: "SMALL STEADY GAINS" on the coin stacks, "TAIL RISK" on the roller, "ONE BIG LOSS" on the inset.

key: Averaging down is a rubber band
name: ch08_rubber_band_averaging
alt: A man keeps stretching a rubber band further, which usually snaps back, until one day it does not and he is left holding a huge stretched band.
scene: A cramped home office of a retail trader in a city apartment at night, a laptop with a red-heavy chart glowing, sticky notes, an empty chai glass. The main subject is a sweating man in his thirties in a crumpled office shirt, standing and stretching an enormous rubber band between his two hands, arms spread nearly to the edges of the frame. Behind him a row of four faded ghost images shows earlier days: each time he stretched a small band a little, it snapped back with a cheerful ping and a coin popped out, and he smiled. In the main image, the band is now five times thicker than in those earlier scenes, stretched to its limit, thin and translucent at the middle with tiny tear marks, and he has added extra loops of band around his wrists, showing he keeps adding size. His face shows strain and denial. A small wall clock and a calendar suggest late night. Cool blue screen light mixed with a warm table lamp, tense mood. Labels: "AVERAGING DOWN" over the stretched band, "USUALLY SNAPS BACK" over the ghost images, "5X SIZE" with an arrow to the thick loops on his wrists.

key: Three thermometers in the same room
name: ch08_three_thermometers
alt: Three different thermometers on one wall all show the same reading, because they are measuring the same room.
scene: A small, plain Indian living room in summer, a ceiling fan turning slowly, a single window with sunlight and a cooler humming in the corner. On the main wall hang three very different-looking thermometers side by side: an old mercury tube on a wooden plaque, a round dial with a needle, and a small digital display. All three point to the same reading, and three short dotted lines from them converge on a single thermometer icon in the centre of the room. Below them, a confident young man in a gym T-shirt and shorts points excitedly at the three of them with a big grin, holding up three fingers as if he has three independent confirmations. Beside him, his older sister in a cotton salwar with a cup of tea gently shakes her head with an amused expression, pointing at the single window and the sun. A cat sleeps on a cane chair in the corner. Bright warm afternoon light and slight heat shimmer, light-hearted mood. Labels: "3 INDICATORS" in a small banner above the three thermometers, and "SAME DATA" above the central converging point.

key: Wait until it stops (the break)
name: ch08_moving_train_wait
alt: A passenger waits on the platform instead of jumping onto a moving train, and steps on only after the train stops, reverses and slows at a station.
scene: A wide view of a busy Indian railway platform with a long blue-and-cream passenger train, overhead electric wires, a yellow station board, tea stalls and porters in red shirts. The scene reads left to right as a sequence. On the far left, a young man in a hoodie with a backpack is mid-leap trying to jump onto the moving train as it pulls out, his feet in the air, a guard waving a red flag and shouting. In the centre, a calm middle-aged woman in a blue saree with a small trolley bag stands well back behind the yellow line, watching; above the train a series of small icons shows the train stopping with brakes squealing, then a dotted arrow showing it beginning to roll slowly in the opposite direction. On the right, the train has slowed to a gentle halt at a second platform marker, doors open, and the same woman calmly steps aboard with her bag, a porter smiling. Pigeons, a hanging station clock and a vendor with a kettle fill in details. Warm morning light with long shadows, orderly and calm mood on the right, comic danger on the left. Labels: "THE BREAK" over the stopping train, "CHANGE OF CHARACTER" over the reversing arrow, "PULLBACK: STEP ON" over the woman boarding.

key: A tent pegged down by guy ropes
name: ch09_tent_guy_ropes
alt: Pushing on a pegged tent makes it spring back, but pulling the pegs one by one lets it be moved and re-pitched.
scene: A camping meadow in the Himalayan foothills at dawn, pine trees, a glacier peak far behind, dew on the grass. In the centre stands an orange dome tent held down by six taut guy ropes running out to metal pegs hammered into the ground. The scene shows two moments side by side. On the LEFT, a young man in a puffer jacket and woollen cap pushes hard against the side of the tent with both hands, grimacing; curved spring-back arrows show the tent bouncing back into place each time. On the RIGHT, a calm woman in her thirties in a fleece and trekking trousers kneels by one rope, carefully pulling a peg out of the soil and holding it up to inspect it; small numbered tags on the remaining pegs show she is working through them in order, and a dotted line from each peg leads to a small inset bubble showing what it was holding (one bubble shows a memory of a big loss, another a parent's warning). In the background a faint dotted outline shows the tent's new position on better flat ground by a stream. Cool pink dawn light, calm reflective mood. Labels: "AFFIRMATION" above the pushing man, "PULL THE ANCHORS" above the kneeling woman, "RE-PITCH" on the dotted new site.

key: Some heads spoil every week
name: ch09_grocer_spoiled_greens
alt: A neighbourhood vegetable seller calmly throws away a few spoiled greens and checks the week's cash box, which shows a profit.
scene: A small corner vegetable shop on a busy Indian residential street in the evening, wooden crates of tomatoes, onions, cabbages and leafy greens on a sloping display, a hanging weighing scale and a string of tube lights. The grocer, a relaxed man in his fifties with a grey stubble, white vest and checked lungi, stands at the side of the shop calmly dropping two wilted lettuce heads into a plastic bin without looking at them, his gaze instead on a battered steel cash box he holds open in his other hand. Inside the cash box is a neat stack of notes, and a tiny paper slip shows a weekly tally with a tick. Behind him a calendar hangs on the wall with seven days ringed in a block. On the left side of the scene, a younger assistant in a cricket jersey kneels dramatically over the bin, clutching his head in despair over the spoiled lettuce, which the grocer clearly finds slightly amusing. Customers with cloth bags browse the crates and a cow wanders past on the street. Warm tube-light glow mixing with dusky blue sky, calm good-humoured mood. Labels: "ONE LOSING TRADE" pointing to the spoiled lettuce, "WEEKLY TILL" on the cash box, "20-TRADE BLOCK" on the ringed calendar.

key: A dam with one crack. Ninety-nine
name: ch09_dam_one_crack
alt: A huge dam with a single crack that widens a little each time water seeps through without disaster.
scene: A massive concrete dam across a river valley in the Western Ghats, seen from downstream at a slight upward angle, the reservoir glinting at the top, green hills on both sides and a small village with tiled roofs far below. The dam wall is clean and solid almost everywhere, but near the centre runs a single thin dark crack with a trickle of water seeping out. Along the crack, three small inset frames arranged in a row show its growth over time: first a hairline with a tiny drip, then a wider crack with a steady stream, and finally a wide split with water spraying out, each frame with a slightly larger trickle. In the foreground a dam inspector in a white hard hat and orange vest, a woman in her forties holding a clipboard, looks up at the crack with a concerned frown, while a careless young engineer beside her shrugs and points to the rest of the solid wall, smiling. A small signboard on the embankment reads "99%". Overcast monsoon light with heavy clouds, quietly ominous mood. Labels: "ONE BAD HABIT" on the crack, "STILL HOLDING" on the solid wall, "WIDER EACH TIME" over the three inset frames.

key: A farmer with good land. Some seasons
name: ch09_farmer_dry_season
alt: A woman farmer stands calmly in a parched field during a failed monsoon, a ledger showing long-run yields in her hand.
scene: A wide rural landscape in the Deccan plateau during a dry year, cracked brown earth in the foreground field, a few stunted millet plants, a dry irrigation channel, and a cloudless pale sky; on the distant horizon, faint green fields hint at better years. In the centre stands a strong, weathered woman farmer in her late forties, wearing a faded green nine-yard saree tucked for work, a towel over her head, holding an old cloth-bound ledger open in one hand and a sickle in the other, looking calmly across the field rather than in despair. Floating above the ledger is a row of small icons: ten bags of grain of different sizes for ten past seasons, mostly large, with two small ones, and a dotted average line running across them. On her left, a granary built of mud and thatch with a padlocked door shows stored sacks through a small window, her reserve for dry years. A pair of bullocks rests under the only tree, and her teenage son brings water in a steel pot. Harsh, hot midday light with heat haze, steady and resilient mood. Labels: "DRY SEASON" over the cracked field, "LONG-RUN YIELD" on the ledger icons, "RESERVES" on the granary.

key: A shortcut through a park
name: ch10_park_shortcut_fenced
alt: A shortcut path worn into a park lawn becomes crowded and is finally fenced off by the city.
scene: A wide aerial three-quarter view of a city park in Bengaluru, with a curving paved official footpath, rain trees, benches and flowerbeds. A diagonal path has been worn into the grass, shown in three stages across the image from left to right. LEFT: a single office-goer in a blue shirt with a laptop bag steps across the lawn, a faint trail behind him, the grass barely flattened. CENTRE: the shortcut is now a clear brown dirt track packed with people — joggers, students, a vendor pushing a cart, a woman with a pram — jostling and bumping into each other, the path widened and muddy, everyone slowed down. RIGHT: a municipal worker in an orange vest and a supervisor with a clipboard have installed a low green railing across the shortcut with a small signboard, and the crowd is now funnelled back onto the official path. A newspaper lying on a bench in the foreground shows a headline graphic of the path as if it had been published. Bright morning light filtering through trees, mildly humorous mood. Labels: "EDGE FOUND" over the single walker, "CROWDED OUT" over the jammed shortcut, "EDGE GONE" on the fence.

key: The board jumps up and down all day
name: ch10_gold_shop_bid_ask
alt: In a jewellery shop, a display board flips between a buying price and a selling price for gold as customers alternately sell and buy, though gold's value never changes.
scene: A traditional Indian jewellery shop interior with glass counters, red velvet trays of gold bangles and chains, a mirrored wall and a small shrine with a lamp. Behind the counter, a smiling shopkeeper in his sixties wearing a white shirt and a tilak sits beside a digital price board mounted on the wall. The scene shows the board flipping: on the left side of the counter, a young woman in a salwar sells an old gold chain and the board above her shows a lower number with a small red down-arrow; on the right side, a middle-aged man in a kurta buys a gold coin and the board above him shows a higher number with a small green up-arrow. A dotted zig-zag line connects the two price readings and continues across the wall like a jagged trail, while a single gold bar in a glass case in the middle sits perfectly still with a steady flat line beside it. A small pile of coins on the counter is being swept into the shopkeeper's drawer between the two customers. Warm golden shop lighting, bustling and cheerful mood. Labels: "BID" above the left reading, "ASK" above the right reading, "SPREAD COST" on the coins going into the drawer.

key: A crowd at a concert: one person stands
name: ch10_concert_crowd_standing
alt: At an outdoor concert one person stands to see better, everyone behind stands too, and later they all sit down at once.
scene: An outdoor evening music concert in a college ground, a lit stage on the far horizon with a singer and colourful lights, rows of plastic chairs filling the field. The image is split into two moments by a thin vertical line. LEFT moment: a single young man in a yellow T-shirt in the front rows stands up to see better, and a slow wave of people behind him rises row by row — a girl in a denim jacket, an uncle with a phone, a group of friends — drawn as a gradual ripple with small arrows, until in the back rows everyone is standing on tiptoe, still unable to see, stretching their necks and looking frustrated. RIGHT moment: the whole crowd drops back into their chairs all at once, many people simultaneously sitting down with a big collective downward motion arrow, drinks sloshing, one man missing his chair and falling comically. Paper lanterns and strings of fairy lights hang over the ground, and a security guard at the side shrugs. Purple and orange concert lighting with spotlights, lively mood. Labels: "SLOW RISE" over the left wave of standing, "FAST FALL" over the right collapse, "NOBODY SEES BETTER" across the back rows on the left.

key: A lifeguard who swims only when
name: ch10_lifeguard_waits
alt: A lifeguard sits on a tall chair waiting and only swims when someone is drowning, while another exhausts himself swimming laps.
scene: A wide beach scene at Goa in mid-afternoon, golden sand, a red-and-yellow flag fluttering, a wooden lifeguard tower on the left. On the tower sits a relaxed lifeguard in his thirties, red shorts and a white vest, whistle around his neck, binoculars in hand, watching the sea calmly with a water bottle beside him. In a small inset bubble from his tower, the same lifeguard sprints into the waves to reach a swimmer waving for help, shown as his rare moment of action with a strong arrow. On the right side of the frame, a second lifeguard in matching uniform swims laps back and forth endlessly in the surf, shown with a looping dotted path, gasping and exhausted; next to each lap is a small coin-shaped token dropping into the water and sinking, and a tally board on the shore counts his many laps. Tourists lie under umbrellas, a fisherman's boat rests on the sand, and gulls circle above. Bright afternoon light with sparkling water, calm and gently humorous mood. Labels: "WAIT FOR EDGE" by the seated lifeguard, "TRADING EVERY BAR" over the lap swimmer, "COST PER LAP" on the sinking coins.

key: A lift that skipped floors 4 to 6
name: ch11_lift_true_range
alt: An elevator closes at floor 3 overnight and opens at floor 7 the next morning, then travels only to floor 9, while a passenger who stayed inside rode the whole way.
scene: A cutaway view of a tall apartment building's lift shaft with floor numbers 1 to 10 painted on the wall beside it, shown in two moments. On the left, at night, the lift door closes at floor 3, with a night-shift security guard in a blue uniform waving goodbye from the lobby; a moon shows through a small window. In the middle of the shaft, floors 4, 5 and 6 are drawn faded and greyed out, with a dotted arrow jumping straight up past them overnight. On the right, in morning daylight, the lift doors open at floor 7 and then the cabin moves up to floor 9 with a short solid arrow. Inside the cabin, shown through a cut-away window, a sleepy young man in office clothes with a coffee mug has been standing the whole time, a tall bracket beside him spanning from floor 3 all the way to floor 9. A second, shorter bracket next to the morning trip spans only floors 7 to 9. The building has potted plants on landings and a notice board. Contrast of cool night blue on the left and bright morning light on the right, clever explanatory mood. Labels: "GAP" on the skipped floors, "RANGE" on the short bracket, "TRUE RANGE" on the tall bracket.

key: Tasting soup. One spoonful from
name: ch11_tasting_soup_sample
alt: A cook tastes one spoonful from the top of an unstirred pot of soup, while another stirs and tastes several spoonfuls.
scene: A home kitchen in Kolkata with a large aluminium pot of vegetable soup simmering on a gas stove, a window with a small potted plant, steel shelves with jars. The pot is shown in a cutaway so we can see layers: thin clear broth on top, and chunks of potato, carrot and peas sitting at the bottom unmixed. On the left, a young man in a T-shirt and shorts dips a single spoon at the very top surface and tastes it with a puzzled look, a small thought bubble showing a plain watery taste. On the right, his grandmother, in a white cotton saree with a red border and spectacles, stirs the pot thoroughly with a long ladle, swirling arrows showing the vegetables rising, and lines up ten small steel spoons on the counter each with a little sample, nodding with a knowing smile. A flame under the pot is still on, and a small timer shows the soup is still cooking, with fresh vegetables being dropped in by a third hand from the frame edge. Warm, steamy kitchen light, cosy and instructive mood. Labels: "ONE SPOONFUL" above the young man, "STIRRED SAMPLE" over the ten spoons, "STILL COOKING" with an arrow to the flame.

key: A bathroom scale is accurate for people
name: ch11_bathroom_scale_car
alt: A bathroom scale shows a confident number under a small car, though it is far beyond what the scale can measure.
scene: A driveway outside a suburban Indian house in the afternoon, a gate with a nameplate, potted bougainvillea and a parked scooter. In the left foreground, a young woman in a kurta and jeans stands on a small white bathroom scale on the tiled porch, and a speech bubble shows its display giving a sensible reading; she looks satisfied. In the centre, a mischievous teenage boy in a cricket T-shirt and his friend have rolled one front wheel of a small hatchback onto an identical bathroom scale placed on the driveway; the scale is badly squashed and tilted, yet its little digital display still glows with a calm, confident number. A large exclamation mark hovers over the car. On the right, an amused grandfather in a vest and spectacles sits on a cane chair holding a newspaper, peering over it with eyebrows raised, pointing at the scale. A small inset bubble near the scale shows a tiny symbol of a ruler marked with its valid range, with the car far beyond its end. Bright afternoon sun, playful and humorous mood. Labels: "RIGHT TOOL" by the woman on the scale, "OUT OF RANGE" over the car, "STILL GIVES A NUMBER" pointing to the glowing display.

key: Ice-cream sales and drownings rise
name: ch11_icecream_drownings_summer
alt: A hot summer sun drives both an ice-cream cart's queue and crowds at a swimming lake, linking the two only through the heat.
scene: A sunny Indian beach town promenade in peak summer, a huge blazing sun in the top centre of the frame radiating thick heat waves. On the left, a colourful ice-cream pushcart with a striped umbrella and a cheerful vendor in a cap is surrounded by a long queue of children, a mother with a baby and teenagers holding cones and kulfi sticks, sweat on their foreheads. On the right, a lake beach crowded with swimmers splashing, inflatable rings, a lifeguard on a tower blowing a whistle and a small red warning flag. Two dotted arrows run from the sun, one down to the ice-cream cart and one down to the swimmers, showing that heat drives both. A third, thin, crossed-out arrow runs directly between the ice-cream cart and the swimmers with a big red X, showing that ice cream does not cause the swimming accidents. In the foreground, a puzzled young analyst with a laptop on a bench looks at both groups, scratching his head, and a thermometer on a pole reads very high. Bright, saturated midday light and heat shimmer, light-hearted mood. Labels: "SUMMER" on the sun, "HIDDEN DRIVER" on the two dotted arrows, "NOT CAUSE" by the crossed-out arrow.

key: A rubber band and a snowball
name: ch12_rubber_band_snowball
alt: A split scene: a stretched rubber band snapping back, and a snowball growing as it rolls down a slope.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a schoolboy of about eleven in a white shirt and grey shorts sits on a classroom bench and pulls a thick red rubber band far back between his fingers, then a second ghosted moment shows it snapping back toward the middle with a loud ping-burst and motion lines; a curved double arrow shows the stretch out and the return to centre, and his classmate ducks behind a textbook laughing. Classroom details: a blackboard, a ceiling fan, a tiffin box. RIGHT panel: a snowy slope at a Gulmarg-like hill resort with pine trees and a cable car overhead; a girl of about ten in a red woollen cap and puffy jacket gives a small snowball a push at the top, and down the slope the same snowball is shown three more times, each larger, collecting snow and speed, with a widening track behind it, until at the bottom it is a giant ball heading toward a startled family building a snowman. A forward-pointing arrow grows thicker along the track. Bright classroom light on the left, crisp blue-white snow light on the right, playful mood. Labels: "MEAN REVERSION" at the top of the left panel, "RANGE EXPANSION" at the top of the right panel.

key: A river gauge. A stationary river
name: ch12_river_gauge_stationarity
alt: Three river gauges side by side: one steady, one changed for good by an upstream dam, and one rising every monsoon and falling every winter.
scene: A wide landscape showing three parallel rivers flowing from the hills in the background toward the viewer, each with a tall white-and-red striped water-level gauge post standing in the water in the foreground. LEFT river: calm and steady, small even ripples, and a small calendar strip under its gauge shows the water mark at the same height every year. CENTRE river: upstream in the background a large concrete dam has been built across it, and from the dam onward the river is narrower and the water mark on the gauge sits permanently lower, with a bold break line marking the year the dam was built. RIGHT river: shown with a seasonal strip of small scenes — swollen brown monsoon floods with dark clouds and rain, then a calm, low clear river in winter with mist — repeating in a cycle, and a small circular arrow beside its gauge. A local water-board officer in khaki with a notebook stands on the bank in the foreground, a fisherwoman with a net beside her, both looking at the gauges. Soft overcast light with sunlight breaking over the right river, informative mood. Labels: "STATIONARY" on the left gauge, "NON-STATIONARY" on the centre gauge, "CYCLOSTATIONARY" on the right gauge.

key: engineers studied bullet holes on
name: ch12_survivor_bombers
alt: Engineers study bullet holes on returning planes, while the planes hit elsewhere never came back.
scene: An old military airfield at dusk with a hangar, a windsock and a muddy grass runway. In the foreground, three battered old propeller bombers with no markings or insignia are parked, their wings and tails riddled with dotted bullet-hole patterns, but their engines and cockpits clean and untouched. A small team of engineers in overalls with clipboards — a woman with a pencil behind her ear, an older man with a measuring tape, a young apprentice on a ladder — mark the holes with chalk circles. Standing a little apart, a thoughtful statistician in a tweed jacket and glasses points instead at the clean, unmarked engines, a lightbulb above his head. In the background sky, faint ghost silhouettes of several planes that never returned fade away into the clouds, each with holes on its engine areas. A small inset bubble in the corner shows a notepad with a list of stock tickers drawn as plane icons, all of them returned survivors. Warm golden-orange dusk light with long shadows, thoughtful and slightly sombre mood. Labels: "SURVIVORS ONLY" over the parked planes, "MISSING DATA" over the ghost planes, "YOUR STOCK LIST" on the inset.

key: Measuring your height by standing
name: ch12_height_on_boxes
alt: A child is measured each year while standing on a different box, so the chart shows fake jumps, while the honest method measures only growth on the same box.
scene: A cosy Indian family home with a white wall where a child's height is marked in pencil every year beside dates, near a doorframe. The scene shows the same girl at different ages in a row from left to right, growing gradually: a four-year-old in a frock, a six-year-old in a school uniform, an eight-year-old with a ponytail. Under each one is a different wooden box or stool: a low shoe box, a tall plastic crate, a short wooden step, each of a different height, so the pencil marks on the wall leap up and down unevenly, with one huge jump circled in red and labelled with a surprised face. On the right side of the frame, her father, a gentle man in his late thirties in a kurta and spectacles, holds a measuring tape carefully against her while she stands on the same box as last time, noting only the small difference in a notebook, and a neat stack of small blocks beside him shows those true growth pieces added up. Her grandmother watches from a sofa knitting. Warm morning light through lace curtains, tender and lightly humorous mood. Labels: "FAKE JUMP" at the circled leap, "SAME BOX" by the father measuring, "STITCHED GROWTH" on the stack of blocks.

key: Pour two cups of any size into a bucket
name: ch13_cups_into_bucket
alt: Cups of water are poured into a bucket, each new cup equal to the last two combined, and the ratio between neighbouring cups settles near 1.618.
scene: A bright school science lab with wooden benches, a periodic table on the wall and a window onto a playground. On a long bench, a row of steel and glass cups of growing size stands left to right: two small mismatched cups at the start, one tiny and one medium, then each following cup visibly equal to the previous two combined, growing quickly larger until the last is a big jug. Curved arrows show the two previous cups being poured together into the next. A curious girl of about fourteen in a school uniform with two plaits pours the latest jug into a large blue bucket on the floor, while a boy beside her holds a ruler up between the last two cups, and a small inset bubble shows a simple fraction balance on a stand settling on a needle at the same mark. At the far left, a second, ghosted starting row shows two completely different starting cup sizes, but its later cups still converge to the same ratio, connected by a dotted line to the balance. Their science teacher, a woman in her forties in a printed saree and a lab coat, smiles approvingly with arms folded. Clean, bright daylight, curious and discovering mood. Labels: "ADD THE LAST TWO" over the pouring arrows, "RATIO 1.618" on the balance needle.

key: A ball thrown up a staircase
name: ch13_ball_up_staircase
alt: A ball bounces up a long stone staircase, falls back part of the way to a landing, then climbs a longer flight.
scene: A long outdoor stone staircase climbing a hillside to a temple, like at a hill shrine, with brass bells, marigold garlands on the railings and monkeys sitting on the walls. A bright red rubber ball is shown with a dotted trajectory: first bouncing up one full flight of steps from the bottom left to a high point, then rolling back down part of that flight, then bouncing up again to a higher point above the first, continuing toward the top right. Along the side of the first flight, three small coloured flags are planted on particular steps, roughly a third, half and two-thirds of the way down from the top of that flight, and the ball's drop-back stops near one of them. At the bottom, a cheerful boy of about eight in a yellow T-shirt has just thrown the ball, arms outstretched, and his grandfather, in a dhoti and shawl and carrying a pooja basket, watches with a curious frown, holding a measuring string. A temple priest at the top looks down amused. Soft morning light, misty hills behind, playful and curious mood. Labels: "AB" along the first climb, "BC" along the drop-back, "CD" along the second climb.

key: Throw a handful of darts at a wall
name: ch13_darts_painted_target
alt: A man throws darts at a blank wall, then draws a target around the spot where three darts landed close together.
scene: The plain painted side wall of a neighbourhood community hall in a small town, a dusty courtyard in front with a neem tree and a few plastic chairs. Dozens of darts are stuck randomly all over the wall at different heights, scattered without pattern. Near one corner, three of them happen to be close together. A cocky young man in a bright printed shirt and sunglasses pushed up on his head stands with a fat paint brush and a can of red paint, proudly painting concentric target rings around those three darts, while still holding a few more darts in his other hand. Behind him, three friends on the chairs react: one claps, one films on a phone, and an older woman in a saree raises her eyebrows sceptically, pointing to all the other scattered darts across the rest of the wall. A dotted path from the man's hand shows the throws came before the painting. A small sign beside the wall has a chalked number of total darts thrown. Bright afternoon sunlight with crisp shadows from the darts, humorous mood. Labels: "PAINTED AFTER" on the target rings, "RANDOM DARTS" across the scattered darts, "CLUSTER BY CHANCE" by the three darts.

key: If a road has speed bumps at 38 m
name: ch13_speed_bumps_stops
alt: On a road with two speed bumps, stopping cars pile up at those two marks; on a road without bumps the stops are spread evenly.
scene: An aerial top-down view of two parallel straight suburban roads, separated by a grass median with trees, with distance markers painted along the kerbs. UPPER road: two clearly visible yellow-and-black speed bumps cross it at two points, and many small cars — hatchbacks, autorickshaws, a scooter or two — are bunched up just before each bump with brake lights glowing red, forming two clusters; a small stacked bar of car icons is drawn beside each bump showing the pile-up. LOWER road: completely smooth with no bumps, and the same number of vehicles are slowing to a stop at evenly scattered positions along its whole length, with a flat, even row of car icons drawn beside it. In the foreground on the median, a traffic surveyor in her twenties wearing a reflective vest and holding a clipboard and a tally counter clicks as cars stop, and a small inset sketch in her clipboard compares a two-humped stack against a flat stack. Pedestrians wait at a zebra crossing and a tea stall sits on the corner. Clear late-morning light, analytical but friendly mood. Labels: "BUMPS: CLUSTERS" above the upper road, "NO BUMPS: SPREAD" above the lower road.

key: target painted on a moving truck
name: ch14_target_on_truck
alt: An archer aims at a target painted on a moving truck, while a second identical target painted on the road stays where it was yesterday.
scene: A long highway on the Deccan plains at morning, flat fields and a row of windmills in the distance. On the right, a colourful Indian goods truck with painted decorations and a tarpaulin-covered load drives away toward the horizon, motion lines behind its wheels, a large red-and-white bullseye target painted on its tailgate. On the road surface behind it, a little to the left, sits an identical bullseye painted flat on the tarmac, still and fixed, slightly behind the truck's position, with a faint chalk date beside it showing it was painted the day before. In the foreground left, a young archer in a white kurta with a quiver on her back draws a bow, and a dotted line from her arrow tip goes toward the truck's target and wobbles as the truck moves; a second, steady dotted line goes to the fixed road target. A roadside dhaba with charpais and a man pouring tea watches in the background. Bright clear morning light, long shadows across the road, light and clever mood. Labels: "LIVE AVERAGE" on the truck's target, "OFFSET AVERAGE" on the road target.

key: You thought the dog barked at the
name: ch14_dog_doorbell_not_uniform
alt: A dog barks at a postman without a uniform just as loudly, revealing it was the doorbell all along.
scene: A split-panel scene at the front door of a small Indian house with a grilled metal gate, a tulsi plant in a pot and a nameplate, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an Indian postman in a khaki uniform and cap, with a cloth mail bag over his shoulder, presses the doorbell button; a brown-and-white dog behind the gate barks furiously, ears up, with zig-zag bark lines, and a homeowner in her forties peeking from the window points at the uniform with a confident nod. RIGHT panel: the same postman now dressed in a plain checked shirt and jeans, no cap and no bag, presses the same doorbell, and the dog barks exactly as furiously; the homeowner's eyebrows shoot up in surprise. In both panels a bright ring-burst comes out of the doorbell button with sound lines that lead straight to the dog's ears, drawn as a dotted cause arrow. A small cat sits on the boundary wall unimpressed. Bright late-morning sunlight, comic, eye-opening mood. Labels: "UNIFORM?" over the left panel, "DOORBELL!" over the doorbell burst in the right panel, and "REAL CAUSE" on the dotted arrow to the dog.

key: A fishing spot that fed a village
name: ch14_fishing_spot_book
alt: A fishing spot fed a village for decades until a book about it drew crowds and the nets came up nearly empty.
scene: A split-panel scene of the same small cove on the Konkan coast, palm-fringed beach, wooden fishing boats with outriggers and a small whitewashed shrine, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: in an earlier era, a few weathered fishermen in lungis and head-cloths haul a bulging net full of silvery fish onto the sand, smiling, women in cotton sarees carrying baskets heaped with fish on their heads, and a small sign with "66 YEARS" on a post. RIGHT panel: the same cove much later, crowded with many motor boats packed close together, tourists with cameras, and a stall selling a thick book with a picture of the cove on its cover; the fishermen pull up a sagging net holding only two small fish, looking disappointed. At the edge, a thoughtful woman statistician in her thirties with a notebook and laptop on a rock compares two small bar sketches of the catch, one tall and one short. A dotted arrow from the book stall points to the crowded boats. Warm golden light on the left, harsher flat light on the right, nostalgic then sobering mood. Labels: "BEFORE PUBLICATION" over the left panel, "AFTER PUBLICATION" over the right panel, "EDGE DECAY" on the statistician's sketch.

key: Steering a car by looking only in the
name: ch14_rear_view_mirror_driving
alt: A driver steers looking only at the rear-view mirror, fine on a straight road but turning late on a twisting mountain road.
scene: A split-panel scene seen from just behind and above a small white hatchback, divided by a thin vertical line. Both panels show a young man in his late twenties in a blue T-shirt driving with his eyes fixed only on the rear-view mirror, where a small reflected image of the road behind is visible. LEFT panel: a long straight expressway through flat yellow mustard fields, perfectly straight lane markings, the car comfortably centred, the driver relaxed with one hand on the wheel, a tiny green tick near the car. RIGHT panel: a twisting ghat road with sharp hairpin bends, steep drops, a stone parapet and a warning signboard with a curvy arrow symbol; the car is turning left just as the road bends right, wheels skidding toward the parapet, the driver's eyes wide, a curved dotted arrow showing the late reaction and a second arrow showing the road's true direction. Monkeys on the parapet scatter. An inset bubble on the right shows the mirror reflection still showing the bend that was already passed. Bright clear daylight on the left, misty green hills on the right, cautionary and slightly comic mood. Labels: "LAGGING SIGNAL" on the mirror, "STRAIGHT TREND" over the left panel, "CHOPPY MARKET" over the right panel.

key: A dog let off the lead at the park gate
name: ch15_dog_from_park_gate
alt: A dog let off its lead at a park gate wanders randomly, and because its first steps went west, the gate stays the farthest east point it ever reaches.
scene: A wide top-down view of a large city park like Cubbon Park with winding paths, rain trees, a pond and lawns, a tall iron park gate at the far right (east) edge of the frame and a compass rose in the corner marking north, south, east and west. Just inside the gate, a smiling woman in her thirties in a kurta and sneakers has just unclipped the lead from a lively black-and-white mongrel dog, holding the empty lead in one hand. From the gate, a long meandering dotted path traces the dog's hour-long wander across the park: it first heads left (west), then loops around trees, sniffs at a bench, chases pigeons near the pond and circles a children's slide, but never once comes back further right than the gate. Small clock icons along the path mark minutes of the hour. A tall dotted vertical line drawn straight down through the gate shows that every point of the path lies to its left. A few joggers, a peanut vendor and a family on a mat appear along the paths. Soft morning light filtering through the trees, playful and curious mood. Labels: "START = EDGE" by the gate, "RANDOM WALK" along the dotted path, "FARTHEST EAST" on the vertical line.
