key: works whether you wear it on your wrist
name: ch15_lucky_charm_everywhere
alt: A lucky charm is worn on the wrist, ankle and in a pocket on different days, and the result is the same every time, showing the charm is not the cause.
scene: A cheerful four-panel grid set in an Indian college hostel room with a cricket poster, a study table and a steel trunk. In each panel the same young student, about nineteen, in a different coloured T-shirt, sits at the desk taking an exam practice paper, and each time ends with the same big green tick at the top of his paper. TOP LEFT: a black thread charm tied on his wrist, wall calendar showing "MON". TOP RIGHT: the charm tied around his ankle, calendar showing "THU". BOTTOM LEFT: the charm tucked into his shirt pocket. BOTTOM RIGHT: the charm forgotten on the bed behind him while he still gets the same tick. Running underneath all four panels is one common detail drawn identically: an open textbook with a bookmark at the starting page and a small pencil starting line, highlighted with a soft glow. His roommate in the background of the last panel lounges on a bunk and laughs, pointing at the charm on the bed. Warm desk-lamp lighting, light-hearted and witty mood. Labels: "CHARM ANYWHERE" across the top of the grid, "SAME RESULT" by the ticks, "EVERY BAR STARTS SOMEWHERE" under the glowing starting line.

key: A ball bouncing randomly in a corridor
name: ch15_ball_in_corridor
alt: A ball bouncing randomly in a long corridor is usually caught in the middle by a snapshot and rarely touches either end wall.
scene: A long, narrow school corridor viewed from the side in a cutaway, with green-painted walls, a row of wooden classroom doors, notice boards and a ceiling fan, two solid end walls at the far left and far right. A small bright yellow tennis ball bounces along the corridor floor, and its random path is shown as a dense tangled dotted line that zigs back and forth mostly in the middle stretch, only rarely reaching close to either end wall. Below the corridor, a strip of floor tiles has been tinted like a heat map: deeply shaded in the middle where the ball spends most of its time, and very lightly shaded near both ends. Above the corridor, three small snapshot frames, like photos clipped to a string, each catch the ball somewhere near the middle. A curious schoolgirl of about twelve in a blue pinafore stands near the middle holding up a small camera, while a peon in khaki with a broom looks on from a classroom door. Afternoon light streaming in through the barred windows, playful and explanatory mood. Labels: "USUALLY MIDDLE" over the dark middle tiles, "RARELY AN END" near each light end, and "RANDOM SNAPSHOT" over the clipped photos.

key: Toss a fair coin all day and keep score
name: ch15_coin_toss_best_moment
alt: A man tosses a coin all day on a scoreboard, and his best moment is most likely to come very early or very late, rarely in the middle.
scene: A shaded village courtyard under a large banyan tree, a wooden bench and a blackboard on an easel. A retired schoolteacher in his sixties, wearing a white kurta, a Nehru cap and round glasses, sits on the bench tossing a silver coin into the air with his thumb, a small tin of chalk beside him. On the blackboard, a long row of tally marks runs from left (morning, a small rising sun icon) to right (evening, a setting sun icon), with a running score line drawn as a gentle chalk path wandering up and down. Above the blackboard, a soft U-shaped bowl curve is drawn in chalk across the same time axis, high at the far left and far right and low in the middle. Two small gold stars are pinned at the very beginning and very end of the board, and a small grey star sits faintly in the middle with a question mark. A group of three village children in school uniforms sit cross-legged on the ground watching the coin spin, and a goat nibbles nearby. Dappled afternoon light through the banyan leaves, relaxed and curious mood. Labels: "BEST SCORE: EARLY" near the left star, "OR LATE" near the right star, "RARELY MIDDLE" by the grey star.
